lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Romans in Britain
lesson.summary: Learn how the Romans invaded Britain and changed towns, roads, buildings and beliefs.
learning_objectives: Describe the Roman invasion of Britain
Explain how towns and roads changed life
Say what changed and what stayed the same

standards.text: The Roman Empire and its impact on Britain: invasion, resistance, Romanisation, towns and roads

success_criteria: I can say when and why the Romans came
I can describe Roman towns and roads
I can give an example of change and continuity
lesson.real_life: UK heritage visits to Bath, York or Hadrian's Wall, and comparing Roman forts with forts in Pakistan such as Rohtas, as examples of empires.

warm_up.prompt: In which country did the Romans begin?
What did Romans build for travel?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how did Roman rule change life in Britain?
blocks.say: Today we travel back almost 2,000 years to see how the Romans changed Britain.

blocks.alt: A green pool surrounded by stone columns and balconies in a historic bathing complex, with a few visitors around the edge
blocks.caption: The Roman Baths in Bath, England.
blocks.credit: Photo by Hulki Okan Tabak on Unsplash
blocks.say: These are the Roman Baths in Bath, England. Romans built them about 1,900 years ago.

blocks.markdown: An **invasion** is when an army enters another land to take control.
blocks.say: The Romans came from Rome, a city in Italy. Their empire was large and powerful.

blocks.markdown: **CE** means Common Era. Years count forwards from year 1.
blocks.say: In 43 CE Emperor Claudius sent about 40,000 soldiers across the sea to Britain.

scenes.caption: The crossing.
scenes.say: Roman ships sailed from Gaul, across the sea to Britain.

scenes.caption: A legion.
scenes.say: A Roman legion was a group of about 5,000 soldiers.

scenes.caption: Marching.
scenes.say: The army marched north and built forts and roads.

question.prompt: In which year did the Roman invasion of Britain begin?

blocks.markdown: A **rebellion** is a fight against those in charge.
blocks.say: Not everyone accepted Roman rule. Boudica was queen of the Iceni tribe.

blocks.markdown: Britons did not all think alike. Some fought and some made peace.
blocks.say: About 60 CE she led a rebellion. Her army burned towns, but the Romans won in the end.

scenes.caption: Boudica.
scenes.say: Boudica led the Iceni in the east of Britain.

scenes.caption: Attacks.
scenes.say: Her army attacked Roman towns such as Colchester and London.

scenes.caption: Defeat.
scenes.say: The Roman army defeated her and Roman rule continued.

question.prompt: Everyone in Britain accepted Roman rule at once.

blocks.title: Imran on a Roman road
blocks.transcript: Imran walks along a straight Roman road near Bath. The road has layers of stone and gravel. In the town he finds the forum, a market square. Next he finds the hot baths where Romans met friends. A mosaic floor is made of tiny stone pieces. He learns that Britons and Romans mixed their ways. Imran visits the museum to learn more. Imran wants to protect this heritage for everyone.
blocks.caption: Imran walks a Roman road near Bath and finds baths, a forum and mosaic floors.

points: Claudius sent an army in 43 CE
blocks.say: Let us remember. The Romans invaded in 43 CE, and some Britons resisted.

blocks.markdown: A **forum** is a market square and meeting place.
blocks.say: Romans built towns with a forum in the middle. The forum was a market and meeting place.

blocks.markdown: Baths were also a place to meet friends.
blocks.say: Many towns also had public baths. People went there to wash, talk and relax.

scenes.caption: The forum.
scenes.say: The forum had shops, offices and a hall for the town council.

scenes.caption: Baths.
scenes.say: The baths had hot rooms and cold pools.

blocks.markdown: Soldiers built them so the army could march fast.
blocks.say: Roman roads were straight and made of layers of stone and gravel.

blocks.markdown: Trade grew because travel was easier.
blocks.say: Roads also helped traders and travellers. Many modern roads follow Roman routes.

blocks.markdown: **Evidence** is a clue that helps us find out about the past.
blocks.say: Historians use evidence. Evidence includes ruins, coins, pottery and writing.

blocks.alt: A grassy crag with a stone wall running across a hillside, a paved footpath and a stormy grey sky
blocks.caption: Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland, northern England.
blocks.credit: Photo by Gabe Fender on Unsplash
blocks.say: Hadrian's Wall in northern England is a ruin you can still visit.

scenes.caption: Finds.
scenes.say: Archaeologists dig up coins, pots and jewellery.

scenes.caption: A wall.
scenes.say: Hadrian's Wall was begun in 122 CE to guard the north.

scenes.caption: Mosaics.
scenes.say: Mosaic floors show the art in rich Roman houses.

question.explanation: A coin is a clue from the past.

blocks.alt: A close-up of an ancient floor made of small stone tiles in swirls, bands and leaf patterns in cream, black and red
blocks.caption: A Roman-style mosaic floor made of tiny stone pieces.
blocks.credit: Photo by Adrien Antal on Unsplash
blocks.say: Mosaics and ruins show that Roman ways spread. Many Britons copied some of them.

blocks.title: Roman clues
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Not all changes were the same. Some people adopted Roman habits. Others kept old ways.

scenes.caption: New habits.
scenes.say: Some Britons wore Roman clothes and learned Latin.

scenes.caption: Old ways.
scenes.say: Others kept Celtic homes and customs.

scenes.caption: A mix.
scenes.say: At Bath, people honoured Sulis, a local goddess, together with Minerva.

question.prompt: Ruins can tell us nothing about the past.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Evidence helps us see how Roman and British ways mixed.

blocks.markdown: **Continuity** means things staying the same. **Change** means things becoming different.
blocks.say: Before the Romans, Celtic tribes lived in round houses. After 43 CE, some lived in towns.

scenes.caption: Before.
scenes.say: Celtic families lived in round houses in villages and farms.

scenes.caption: After.
scenes.say: Romans built towns, forts, villas and roads.

scenes.caption: Still the same.
scenes.say: Many farmers still grew crops in the same fields.

question.prompt: Which of these stayed the same?

blocks.markdown: People in Roman Britain came from many places.
blocks.say: The Ivory Bangle Lady lived in York about 1,700 years ago. She came from North Africa.

scenes.caption: Many places.
scenes.say: Roman Britain had soldiers and traders from Gaul, Spain and Africa.

scenes.caption: Different choices.
scenes.say: Some Britons adopted Roman life. Others protested.

scenes.caption: A mix.
scenes.say: Romano-British means a person in Britain with a mix of both ways.
